mcqs.question: How does the review define hyperventilation syndrome within dysfunctional breathing?

options.A: Symptoms related to respiratory alkalosis and symptoms independent of hypocapnia
options.B: Only a panic attack with normal carbon dioxide and no breathing change

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Symptoms related to respiratory alkalosis and symptoms independent of hypocapnia
mcqs.explanation: Hyperventilation syndrome is associated with symptoms both related to respiratory alkalosis and independent of hypocapnia.

sourceRefs.excerpt: 1) Hyperventilation syndrome: associated with symptoms both related to respiratory alkalosis and independent of hypocapnia.

mcqs.question: What is the second pattern in the proposed classification?

options.A: Periodic deep sighing, with frequent sighing and an irregular pattern
options.B: Cheyne–Stokes breathing from heart failure only

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Periodic deep sighing, with frequent sighing and an irregular pattern
mcqs.explanation: Periodic deep sighing is frequent sighing with an irregular breathing pattern.

sourceRefs.excerpt: 2) Periodic deep sighing: frequent sighing with an irregular breathing pattern.

mcqs.question: What does thoraco-abdominal asynchrony mean in this classification?

options.A: Delay between rib-cage and abdominal contraction, with ineffective mechanics
options.C: Diaphragmatic paralysis proven on every case

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Delay between rib-cage and abdominal contraction, with ineffective mechanics
mcqs.explanation: There is delay between rib-cage and abdominal contraction, resulting in ineffective breathing mechanics.

sourceRefs.excerpt: 5) Thoraco-abdominal asynchrony: where there is delay between rib cage and abdominal contraction resulting in ineffective breathing mechanics.

mcqs.question: When does the review consider thoracic-dominant breathing dysfunctional?

options.A: When it occurs without somatic disease, and it results in dyspnoea

mcqs.correctAnswerText: When it occurs without somatic disease, and it results in dyspnoea
mcqs.explanation: It can occur in somatic disease; without disease it may be considered dysfunctional and results in dyspnoea.

sourceRefs.excerpt: 3) Thoracic dominant breathing: can often manifest in somatic disease, if occurring without disease it may be considered dysfunctional and results in dyspnoea.

mcqs.question: What muscle pattern defines forced abdominal expiration in the review?

options.A: Inappropriate and excessive abdominal muscle contraction to aid expiration

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Inappropriate and excessive abdominal muscle contraction to aid expiration
mcqs.explanation: Patients use inappropriate and excessive abdominal muscle contraction to aid expiration.

sourceRefs.excerpt: 4) Forced abdominal expiration: these patients utilise inappropriate and excessive abdominal muscle contraction to aid expiration.
